Dual-representation sign reversal of the polynomial and canonical transgression

sources.title: Adel Bilal, Lectures on Anomalies (full lecture notes)

contents.name: Further conventions: signature, chirality matrix, and epsilon tensor (§2.4)

source_review.read_extent: Read §2.4 in full (printed p. 9), including the (-+++) signature, gamma5 definition, and epsilon convention.
source_review.supports: The item adopts the same Minkowski signature and gamma5 convention for positive chirality.
source_review.limitations: The source convention is recorded only to fix signs; no epsilon-component formula is used as a separate physical claim.

contents.name: Triangle diagram with chiral fermions only: Pauli–Villars subtraction and the consistent one-loop anomaly (§§5.2.2–5.2.3)

source_review.read_extent: Read §§5.2.2–5.2.3 through equations (5.32)–(5.47), printed pp. 33–39: the chiral determinant issue, opposite-statistics Pauli–Villars subtraction, large-mass limit, anomalous triangle term, and Wess–Zumino completion.
source_review.supports: The Pauli–Villars triangle calculation supports the selected consistent positive-chirality coefficient; the B example displays a single-species nonzero cubic polynomial under the same input.
source_review.limitations: The item states the determinant-to-descent law as a selected input; it does not claim Bilal proves a nonperturbative determinant construction or a general continuum measure.

contents.name: Left-handed particles versus right-handed antiparticles and conjugate representation traces (§7.1)

source_review.read_extent: Read §7.1 in full (printed pp. 45–47), including the chirality and charge-conjugation sign comparison.
source_review.supports: This checks the chirality/representation convention used by the conjugate-pair lemma and theorem.
source_review.limitations: The actual polynomial cancellation is proved in the local item by transposition; no antiparticle reinterpretation is needed.

contents.name: Gauge groups and representations with nonzero cubic anomaly coefficient (§7.2)

source_review.read_extent: Read §7.2 in full (printed pp. 48–50), including the complex-conjugate representation trace and cubic coefficient.
source_review.supports: The trace sign reversal and representation-dependent cubic coefficient agree with the direct matrix proof.
source_review.limitations: The lemma proves the exact selected SU(3)×U(1) identity directly; no group-classification conclusion is required.

contents.name: Characteristic classes, Chern–Simons forms, and descent equations (§8.3)

source_review.read_extent: Read §§8.3.1–8.3.3 in full (printed pp. 63–68), covering characteristic classes, the Chern–Simons transgression, and descent.
source_review.supports: This supports the transgression and local descent conventions used in the data and examples.
source_review.limitations: The exact K3 differentiation and counterterm variation are proved in the example; the proof does not rely on a diagram.

contents.name: Reformulation in terms of BRST cohomology and local counterterm equivalence (§9.2)

source_review.read_extent: Read §9.2 in full (printed pp. 71–72), including BRST closure and the local-counterterm equivalence relation.
source_review.supports: The local quotient and counterterm shift are used in the definition and proved directly in the mathematical lemma.
source_review.limitations: The source treats local functionals in its gauge-theory setting; the item explicitly instantiates the quotient on the selected background jet algebra.

contents.name: Determining the higher-order terms of the anomaly in d=4 (§9.3)

source_review.read_extent: Read §9.3 in full (printed pp. 73–75), including the Wess–Zumino consistency argument that fixes higher-order terms from the triangle coefficient.
source_review.supports: This supports treating the full consistent descent as the selected source-backed one-loop input.
source_review.limitations: No separate triangle or Ward-identity computation is claimed in the batch theorem.

contents.name: Descent equations for anomalies in d=2r dimensions (§9.4)

source_review.read_extent: Read §9.4 in full (printed pp. 75–77), including the BRST descent, representation additivity, and anomaly-polynomial relation.
source_review.supports: This supports the use of a fixed linear consistent descent and sum over Weyl species.
source_review.limitations: The vanishing for the selected pair follows from the local trace identity, not from a general anomaly-cancellation assertion.

contents.name: Gauge anomalies in 2r dimensions: anti-Hermitian normalization (§10.4)

source_review.read_extent: Read §10.4 in full (printed pp. 87–88), including equations (10.49)–(10.54) and the degree-six component.
source_review.supports: This fixes the anti-Hermitian connection convention and 2π[tr exp(-iF/(2π))]6 normalization used by the cubic-polynomial definition.
source_review.limitations: The theorem makes no index-theorem or global-anomaly claim.

contents.name: Mixed gauge-gravitational anomalies (§11.3.2)
contents.reason: The assigned model uses flat spacetime and only the pure gauge degree-six polynomial; no gravitational background or mixed gauge-gravitational claim is included.

source_review.read_extent: Read §11.3.2 (printed pp. 92–94), including the separate mixed gauge-gravitational polynomial term.
source_review.supports: The source confirms that mixed gravitational terms are separate data from the pure gauge polynomial.
source_review.limitations: This distinct term is explicitly excluded in the assigned matching-data statement.

contents.name: Stora–Zumino algebraic formalism (§2.1)

source_review.read_extent: Read §2.1 in full (printed pp. 25–29), including invariant polynomials and Chern–Simons transgression.
source_review.supports: This is an independent formal treatment of the invariant-polynomial starting point used for the selected descent.
source_review.limitations: Only the local formalism is imported; bundle-global questions are outside the batch model.

contents.name: Stora–Zumino descent equations (§2.2)

source_review.read_extent: Read §2.2 in full (printed pp. 30–33), including the ghost-number descent and consistent-anomaly condition.
source_review.supports: This independently supports a common linear descent from the invariant polynomial.
source_review.limitations: The item fixes its own BRST signs and does not substitute Alvarez’s notation without translation.

contents.name: Representation-index additivity and conjugate-representation sign (§2.2)

source_review.read_extent: Read the representation-index/additivity passage in §2.2 (printed pp. 32–33), including equations (2.98)–(2.100).
source_review.supports: This is an independent check that the cubic index is additive and reverses under conjugation.
source_review.limitations: The exact dual Chern–Simons sign is proved locally in the batch lemma.

contents.name: Anomaly cancellation in the Standard Model (§2.3)
contents.reason: The batch treats only the selected SU(3)×U(1)V conjugate pair; the Standard Model field content and charge assignments are not used.

source_review.read_extent: Read §2.3 in full (printed pp. 34–35), including the listed Standard Model charge cancellations.
source_review.supports: This provides a separate worked cancellation example in the source.
source_review.limitations: No Standard Model fields, charge table, or phenomenological conclusion is imported into the assigned items.

contents.name: Consistent versus covariant anomalies and the Bardeen–Zumino counterterm (§2.4)

source_review.read_extent: Read §2.4 in full (printed pp. 36–38), including the local counterterm relation and the consistency distinction.
source_review.supports: This supports keeping the item’s representative shift separate from a claim about removal of the full anomaly class.
source_review.limitations: The covariant anomaly itself is not called the consistent BRST anomaly in the batch.
